The <form>-wrapped test must go from 'a direct child of the H2' to 'the control exists' failing outright.

name: the insertion point is button:last-of-type again
why: Defect 2 verbatim. On an <h3> carrying a sub-table filter that selector resolves to #mb-stf-<col>-clear, several levels deep, so the control lands inside span.mb-stf-input-wrap. The multi-table test asserts the parent IS the h3, so it must fail. Note the single-table test can also see this, which is why both are listed separately below.

why: The same mutation seen from the other page shape: on the <form>-wrapped h2 the selector resolves into #mb-filter-container, so the control is no longer a direct child of the heading. Listed separately because the two page shapes fail it for different reasons and a fix for one would not necessarily fix the other.

name: the control is inserted at the heading's end instead of its control run
why: The plausible simplification: 'just append it to the heading'. It survives every existence check and puts the control after the global filter bar on an h2 — outside the row of controls it is meant to join, and out of reach of updateH2Count()'s re-anchor ordering. The position assertion (immediately after .mb-row-count-stat) is the only thing that sees it.

name: the multi-table <h2> guard is dropped
why: An honest expect: "pass". The guard keeps a per-table control off the PAGE heading, which belongs to #mb-rel-retry-global. No committed multi-table fixture can exercise it: caaFindHeaderForTable() tries findH3ForTable() first, and on every multi-table fixture here renderGroupedTable() puts an h3.mb-toggle-h3 immediately before each table, so the h2 fallback is never reached and removing the guard changes nothing. Reproducing it needs a multi-table page whose sub-table has no h3 within five element-siblings — which would be a rendering bug in its own right. Recorded rather than left unmentioned.
grep: is a direct child of its OWN h3

name: _relTableHasColumn reads the tbody only
why: An honest expect: "pass". The <thead> arm is there because runFilter() REMOVES non-matching rows, so a tbody-only test reports "no column" for a sub-table filtered to nothing and the button would be swept and not come back — these callers do not run on every keystroke. No fixture here filters a sub-table to zero rows and then re-triggers _relCreateRetryButtons(), so the two arms agree throughout and the spec cannot separate them.

name: the per-table guard AND the stray sweep are both dropped
why: The defect reported on 2026-09-21, restored in full: _relCreateRetryButtons()'s loop gated only on the page-wide _relPageHasColumn(), so on a page whose sub-tables differ every one of them got a 🔗⟳. Measured on debug/place-performances-bug.html: 4 strays of 5 sub-tables, each offering to re-fetch a column that is not there. BOTH edits are needed to reproduce it — see the two singles below.

name: only the per-table loop guard is dropped
why: An honest expect: "pass", and mutation-testing is what established it. The sweep that follows removes the stray the loop just created, so the guard's removal is invisible here. Keep the guard anyway: it is what stops the button being built and inserted at all, and the sweep is a cleanup for the OTHER creation site, not a substitute. Pinned as a pair by the combined entry above.

name: only the stray sweep is dropped
why: The other half of the pair, and also an honest expect: "pass" — the loop guard covers for it on this fixture. The sweep exists for what the loop cannot reach: a button left by _artCreateOrUpdateRetryButton() (which runs from the artwork pipeline, off in every fixture) or by a table that has since lost its column.

name: the sweep is not restricted to the per-table numeric id form
why: mb-rel-retry-global and mb-rel-retry-failed share the prefix and are NOT per-table. With the digits relaxed, Number('global') is NaN, _tbls[NaN] is undefined, _relTableHasColumn(undefined) is false — and the sweep deletes the page-wide controls. The multi-table test asserts #mb-rel-retry-global is present on the page h2.
